title: introduce-resilience-tokens-and-hedged-request-protocol
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Services and client SDKs currently implement retries, timeouts, and hedged requests inconsistently. This causes uneven SLO adherence across regions, duplicate work in service teams, and client-side behaviors that can exacerbate overload during partial failures (thundering-herd). We need a unified contract so SDKs, runtime routing, and control-plane can coordinate: 1) which requests are safe to retry, 2) how hedging budgets are consumed, and 3) how load-shedding and circuit breakers interact with retries and hedges.

Proposal summary: Introduce a compact "resilience token" that clients attach to each RPC. The token encodes request SLO class (latency target / priority), an optional idempotency key, and a hedging budget hint. The runtime and edge routing layer will use the token to apply per-customer retry budgets, region-aware hedging policies, and load-shedding rules. SDK changes will offer a standard API surface: createResilienceToken({slo_class, idempotency_key?, hedge_policy?}) and useResilienceToken(token). Hedging protocol: clients may send a primary request and schedule hedges after an adaptive window; the runtime will reject hedges when a per-customer hedge-quota is exhausted or when a downstream circuit breaker marks the path as degraded. Backoff governor: unify to an SLO-class-aware algorithm (initial_delay = f(p50_latency, slo), jittered exponential up to a max cap), with client-observable headers describing remaining retry budget.

Why tokens: they reduce namespace pollution (single header), enable observability correlation (token ID maps to request class), and allow runtime to make smarter decisions (e.g., favor regional fallback for high-priority tokens).

Components to change:
- SDKs (JS, Python, Go): add resilience token creation helpers, default hedging implementation, expose remainingRetryBudget metric.
- Runtime router: read and validate token, enforce hedge budgets, annotate traces with token id.
- Console/observability: dashboards for token-class latency, per-customer hedge/quota consumption, and hedged-request impact on cost.
- Docs and runbooks: migration guide for services, recommended idempotency semantics, and emergency rollback steps.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Backward compatibility: token header is optional; if absent, runtime applies legacy behavior (conservative no-hedge for non-idempotent requests).
- Complexity: tokens add control-plane surface and quotas to track per-customer. We'll implement a soft rollout and telemetry-first approach.
- Security: tokens do not contain secrets. They are opaque IDs or signed minimal assertions. Security review required for token signing and quota enforcement paths.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose createResilienceToken and useResilienceToken helpers in JS, Python, and Go
Runtime honors token SLO class and enforces per-customer hedge budgets in non-blocking fashion
Hedged requests are rejected by router when downstream circuit breaker marks path degraded
Console has a token-class dashboard showing latency P50/P95, retry/hedge counts, and per-customer budget consumption
Migration guide published and two pilot services adopt tokens with zero-production-incident rollout
Automated e2e test simulating regional outage demonstrates controlled hedging (no uncontrolled thundering-herd)
implementation_notes: Phase 1: implement token parser and honor basic fields (slo_class, idempotency_key, token_id) in router; add metrics for hedge attempts and budget rejections. Phase 2: SDK helpers and hedging client logic with adaptive delay. Phase 3: quota service and signed token support for private deployments. Feature-flag rollout per customer and per-region. Avoid hedging to regions under active failover unless token SLO class == critical. Provide compatibility header fallback for legacy clients.
migration_plan: 1) Add metrics and do not enforce budgets (telemetry-only) for 1 week. 2) Pilot with 2 internal services (search and embeddings) with feature flag. 3) Enforce budgets for pilot customers. 4) Gradual rollout to all services over 8 weeks with opt-out for high-risk customers. 5) Finalize docs and flip global opt-in flag.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect idempotency interpretation leads to duplicate work; Mitigation: default conservative behavior (no automatic retries for requests without explicit idempotency key) and strong guidance in SDK. Risk: quota enforcement causes request drops; Mitigation: telemetry-first rollout and burst allowances during ramp. Risk: increased control-plane load for per-customer budgeting; Mitigation: sample-based accounting and soft-limits before hard rejection.
